column3: The Hebrew says “on this day,” without expressly identifying it as the same day of the month as the departure.
The Hebrew repeats their camping: they camped in the wilderness, and Israel camped before the mountain.
The Hebrew explicitly says “also in you” in the promise of enduring trust.
The Hebrew says the mountain’s “edge,” rather than specifically its base.
The Hebrew says they may “go up on the mountain,” rather than merely approach it.
The Hebrew says God answered “with a voice” or “with a sound,” without expressly identifying thunder.
The Hebrew repeats the LORD’s name as the one calling Moses.
The Hebrew retains the image of many “falling.”
The Hebrew separately commands Moses to descend and then ascend with Aaron, rather than simply “bring Aaron with you.”
